sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca brahmacaryaṃ paraṃ tāta madhumāṃsasya varjanam maryādāyāṃ sthito dharmaḥ śamaḥ śaucasya lakṣaṇam
english: Bhīṣma said: Chastity is the highest course, dear son, and the renunciation of honey and meat; dharma abides within bounds, and tranquillity is the mark of purity.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kasmin kāle cared dharmaṃ kasmin kāle 'rtham ācaret kasmin kāle sukhī ca syāt tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: At what time should one pursue dharma, at what time pursue wealth, and at what time enjoy pleasure? Tell me this, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca kālyam arthaṃ niṣeveta tato dharmam anantaram paścāt kāmaṃ niṣeveta na ca gacchet prasaṅgitām
english: Bhīṣma said: In the early hours let him attend to wealth, then immediately after to dharma; afterward let him attend to pleasure, yet never give himself over to attachment.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāṃś cābhimanyeta gurūṃś cāpy abhipūjayet sarvabhūtānulomaś ca mṛduśīlaḥ priyaṃvadaḥ
english: Let him hold the brāhmaṇas in honour and revere his elders; gentle toward all beings, soft of nature, and kindly in speech.

sanskrit: adhikāre yad anṛtaṃ rājagāmi ca paiśunam guroś cālīkakaraṇaṃ samaṃ tad brahmahatyayā
english: Falsehood in the exercise of office, slander carried to the king, and deceit practised against one's teacher—each of these is equal to the slaying of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: praharen na narendreṣu na gāṃ hanyāt tathaiva ca bhrūṇahatyāsamaṃ caitad ubhayaṃ yo niṣevate
english: Let him not strike at kings, nor likewise slay a cow; he who indulges in either of these does what is equal to the killing of an embryo.

sanskrit: nāgniṃ parityajej jātu na ca vedān parityajet na ca brāhmaṇam ākrośet samaṃ tad brahmahatyayā
english: Let him never abandon the sacred fire, nor forsake the Vedas, nor revile a brāhmaṇa—for that too is equal to the slaying of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kīdṛśāḥ sādhavo viprāḥ kebhyo dattaṃ mahāphalam kīdṛśānāṃ ca bhoktavyaṃ tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What kind of brāhmaṇas are the virtuous ones, gifts to whom bear great fruit, and of what kind are those whose food may be eaten? Tell me this, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca akrodhanā dharmaparāḥ satyanityā dame ratāḥ tādṛśāḥ sādhavo viprās tebhyo dattaṃ mahāphalam
english: Bhīṣma said: Free from anger, devoted to dharma, ever truthful, delighting in self-restraint—such are the virtuous brāhmaṇas; a gift given to them bears great fruit.

sanskrit: amāninaḥ sarvasahā dṛṣṭārthā vijitendriyāḥ sarvabhūtahitā maitrās tebhyo dattaṃ mahāphalam
english: Free from conceit, all-enduring, having perceived the truth, their senses subdued, friendly and devoted to the welfare of all beings—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

sanskrit: alubdhāḥ śucayo vaidyā hrīmantaḥ satyavādinaḥ svakarmaniratā ye ca tebhyo dattaṃ mahāphalam
english: Free from greed, pure, learned, modest, truthful in speech, and intent upon their own duty—a gift given to such men bears great fruit.

sanskrit: sāṅgāṃś ca caturo vedān yo 'dhīyīta dvijarṣabhaḥ ṣaḍbhyo nivṛttaḥ karmabhyas taṃ pātram ṛṣayo viduḥ
english: That bull among the twice-born who has studied the four Vedas with their auxiliary sciences, and who has turned away from the six base occupations—him the seers know to be a worthy recipient.

sanskrit: ye tv evaṃguṇajātīyās tebhyo dattaṃ mahāphalam sahasraguṇam āpnoti guṇārhāya pradāyakaḥ
english: Those who are endowed with such qualities—a gift given to them bears great fruit; the giver to one worthy by his merits gains a thousandfold reward.

sanskrit: prajñāśrutābhyāṃ vṛttena śīlena ca samanvitaḥ tārayeta kulaṃ kṛtsnam eko 'pīha dvijarṣabhaḥ
english: Endowed with wisdom and sacred learning, with right conduct and good character, a single bull among the twice-born can in this world deliver an entire lineage.

sanskrit: gām aśvaṃ vittam annaṃ vā tadvidhe pratipādayet dravyāṇi cānyāni tathā pretyabhāve na śocati
english: Let him bestow upon such a one a cow, a horse, wealth, or food, and other goods besides; then in the life beyond he shall not grieve.

sanskrit: tārayeta kulaṃ kṛtsnam eko 'pīha dvijottamaḥ kim aṅga punar ekaṃ vai tasmāt pātraṃ samācaret
english: Even one foremost among the twice-born can in this world deliver a whole lineage—how much more, then, a single soul? Therefore let one seek out a worthy recipient.

sanskrit: niśamya ca guṇopetaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ sādhusaṃmatam dūrād ānāyayet kṛtye sarvataś cābhipūjayet
english: And having heard of a brāhmaṇa endowed with virtue and esteemed by the good, let him summon him from afar for the rite and honour him in every way.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śrāddhakāle ca daive ca dharme cāpi pitāmaha icchāmīha tvayākhyātaṃ vihitaṃ yat surarṣibhiḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Concerning the time of the śrāddha, concerning the offering to the gods, and concerning dharma as well, grandfather, I wish to hear from you what has been ordained by the divine seers.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca daivaṃ pūrvāhṇike kuryād aparāhṇe tu paitṛkam maṅgalācārasaṃpannaḥ kṛtaśaucaḥ prayatnavān
english: Bhīṣma said: Let him perform the offering to the gods in the forenoon, but the rite for the ancestors in the afternoon, accomplished in auspicious observances, having performed his purifications, and diligent.

sanskrit: manuṣyāṇāṃ tu madhyāhne pradadyād upapattitaḥ kālahīnaṃ tu yad dānaṃ taṃ bhāgaṃ rakṣasāṃ viduḥ
english: But to men he should give at midday, as is fitting; a gift bestowed out of its proper time—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: laṅghitaṃ cāvalīḍhaṃ ca kalipūrvaṃ ca yat kṛtam rajasvalābhir dṛṣṭaṃ ca taṃ bhāgaṃ rakṣasāṃ viduḥ
english: What has been stepped over, what has been licked, what has been done amid strife, and what has been looked upon by women in their courses—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: avaghuṣṭaṃ ca yad bhuktam avratena ca bhārata parāmṛṣṭaṃ śunā caiva taṃ bhāgaṃ rakṣasāṃ viduḥ
english: What is eaten amid clamour, and what is eaten by one who keeps no vows, O Bhārata, and what has been touched by a dog—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: keśakīṭāvapatitaṃ kṣutaṃ śvabhir avekṣitam ruditaṃ cāvadhūtaṃ ca taṃ bhāgaṃ rakṣasāṃ viduḥ
english: Food into which a hair or an insect has fallen, upon which one has sneezed, which dogs have gazed upon, over which there has been weeping, or which has been shaken about—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: niroṃkāreṇa yad bhuktaṃ saśastreṇa ca bhārata durātmanā ca yad bhuktaṃ taṃ bhāgaṃ rakṣasāṃ viduḥ
english: What is eaten without the sacred syllable Oṃ, and what is eaten with a weapon at hand, O Bhārata, and what is eaten by an evil-souled man—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: parocchiṣṭaṃ ca yad bhuktaṃ paribhuktaṃ ca yad bhavet daive pitrye ca satataṃ taṃ bhāgaṃ rakṣasāṃ viduḥ
english: What is eaten that has been left over by another, and what may have already been partaken of—at the rite for the gods or for the ancestors alike, that portion they ever know to belong to the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: garhitaṃ ninditaṃ caiva pariviṣṭaṃ samanyunā daivaṃ vāpy atha vā paitryaṃ taṃ bhāgaṃ rakṣasāṃ viduḥ
english: What is reviled and condemned, what is served amid wrath, whether at the rite for the gods or for the ancestors—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: mantrahīnaṃ kriyāhīnaṃ yac chrāddhaṃ pariviṣyate tribhir varṇair naraśreṣṭha taṃ bhāgaṃ rakṣasāṃ viduḥ
english: A śrāddha that is served wanting in sacred chants and wanting in proper rites by the three varṇas, O best of men—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: ājyāhutiṃ vinā caiva yat kiṃ cit pariviṣyate durācāraiś ca yad bhuktaṃ taṃ bhāgaṃ rakṣasāṃ viduḥ
english: Whatever is served without the oblation of clarified butter, and what is eaten by men of evil conduct—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: ye bhāgā rakṣasāṃ proktās ta uktā bharatarṣabha ata ūrdhvaṃ visargasya parīkṣāṃ brāhmaṇe śṛṇu
english: Those portions that are declared to belong to the rākṣasas have now been told, O bull of the Bhāratas; henceforth hear the examination of the brāhmaṇa upon the giving away of the gift.

sanskrit: yāvantaḥ patitā viprā jaḍonmattās tathaiva ca daive vāpy atha vā pitrye rājan nārhanti ketanam
english: All those brāhmaṇas who are fallen, and likewise the dull-witted and the mad—at the rite for the gods or for the ancestors, O king, they deserve no invitation.

sanskrit: śvitrī kuṣṭhī ca klībaś ca tathā yakṣmahataś ca yaḥ apasmārī ca yaś cāndho rājan nārhanti satkṛtim
english: The man afflicted with white leprosy, the leper, the eunuch, he who is wasted by consumption, the epileptic, and the blind, O king, deserve no such honour.

sanskrit: cikitsakā devalakā vṛthāniyamadhāriṇaḥ somavikrayiṇaś caiva śrāddhe nārhanti ketanam
english: Physicians, temple priests who serve images for hire, those who keep vows to no purpose, and sellers of the soma—at a śrāddha they deserve no invitation.

sanskrit: gāyanā nartakāś caiva plavakā vādakās tathā kathakā yodhakāś caiva rājan nārhanti ketanam
english: Singers and dancers, acrobats and players of instruments, reciters of tales and prize-fighters, O king, deserve no invitation.

sanskrit: hotāro vṛṣalānāṃ ca vṛṣalādhyāpakās tathā tathā vṛṣalaśiṣyāś ca rājan nārhanti ketanam
english: Those who officiate at the sacrifices of the base-born, and those who instruct the base-born, and likewise the pupils of the base-born, O king, deserve no invitation.

sanskrit: anuyoktā ca yo vipro anuyuktaś ca bhārata nārhatas tāv api śrāddhaṃ brahmavikrayiṇau hi tau
english: The brāhmaṇa who hires another's sacred service and he who is so hired, O Bhārata—neither of these two deserves the śrāddha, for both are sellers of sacred knowledge.

sanskrit: agraṇīr yaḥ kṛtaḥ pūrvaṃ varṇāvaraparigrahaḥ brāhmaṇaḥ sarvavidyo 'pi rājan nārhati ketanam
english: A brāhmaṇa who has been made the leader at the marriage of a man of lower varṇa—though he be versed in all the sciences, O king, he deserves no invitation.

sanskrit: anagnayaś ca ye viprā mṛtaniryātakāś ca ye stenāś ca patitāś caiva rājan nārhanti ketanam
english: Those brāhmaṇas who keep no sacred fires, and those who bear forth the dead for hire, and thieves and the fallen, O king, deserve no invitation.

sanskrit: aparijñātapūrvāś ca gaṇapūrvāś ca bhārata putrikāpūrvaputrāś ca śrāddhe nārhanti ketanam
english: Those of unknown ancestry, and those born of a guild's promiscuous union, O Bhārata, and the sons born of an appointed daughter—at a śrāddha they deserve no invitation.

sanskrit: ṛṇakartā ca yo rājan yaś ca vārdhuṣiko dvijaḥ prāṇivikrayavṛttiś ca rājan nārhanti ketanam
english: The maker of debts, O king, and the twice-born who lives by usury, and he whose livelihood is the selling of living creatures, O king, deserve no invitation.

sanskrit: strīpūrvāḥ kāṇḍapṛṣṭhāś ca yāvanto bharatarṣabha ajapā brāhmaṇāś caiva śrāddhe nārhanti ketanam
english: Those who were once women, and the makers of arrow-shafts, all of them, O bull of the Bhāratas, and brāhmaṇas who do not chant the sāvitrī—at a śrāddha they deserve no invitation.

sanskrit: śrāddhe daive ca nirdiṣṭā brāhmaṇā bharatarṣabha dātuḥ pratigrahītuś ca śṛṇuṣvānugrahaṃ punaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇas who are debarred from the śrāddha and the offering to the gods have been named, O bull of the Bhāratas; now hear again, of giver and receiver alike, who are worthy of favour.

sanskrit: cīrṇavratā guṇair yuktā bhaveyur ye 'pi karṣakāḥ sāvitrījñāḥ kriyāvantas te rājan ketanakṣamāḥ
english: Those who have fulfilled their vows and are endowed with virtues—even if they be tillers of the soil—if they know the sāvitrī and perform the rites, they, O king, are fit to be invited.

sanskrit: kṣātradharmiṇam apy ājau ketayet kulajaṃ dvijam na tv eva vaṇijaṃ tāta śrāddheṣu parikalpayet
english: Even a well-born twice-born who follows the kṣatriya's dharma in battle one may invite; but a trader, dear son, one should never appoint at the śrāddhas.

sanskrit: agnihotrī ca yo vipro grāmavāsī ca yo bhavet astenaś cātithijñaś ca sa rājan ketanakṣamaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa who maintains the agnihotra fire, who dwells in the village, who is no thief and is mindful of guests—he, O king, is fit to be invited.

sanskrit: sāvitrīṃ japate yas tu trikālaṃ bharatarṣabha bhikṣāvṛttiḥ kriyāvāṃś ca sa rājan ketanakṣamaḥ
english: He who chants the sāvitrī at the three junctures of the day, O bull of the Bhāratas, who lives by alms and performs the rites—he, O king, is fit to be invited.

sanskrit: uditāstamito yaś ca tathaivāstamitoditaḥ ahiṃsraś cālpadoṣaś ca sa rājan ketanakṣamaḥ
english: He who rises with the sun and rests at its setting, and likewise rests at its setting and rises with it, who does no harm and has but few faults—he, O king, is fit to be invited.

sanskrit: akalkako hy atarkaś ca brāhmaṇo bharatarṣabha sasaṃjño bhaikṣyavṛttiś ca sa rājan ketanakṣamaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa free from guile and free from idle cavil, O bull of the Bhāratas, possessed of full awareness and living by alms—he, O king, is fit to be invited.

sanskrit: avratī kitavaḥ stenaḥ prāṇivikrayy atho vaṇik paścāc ca pītavān somaṃ sa rājan ketanakṣamaḥ
english: One who was vowless, a gambler, a thief, a seller of living creatures, and a trader, but who afterward has drunk the soma—he, O king, is fit to be invited.

sanskrit: arjayitvā dhanaṃ pūrvaṃ dāruṇaiḥ kṛṣikarmabhiḥ bhavet sarvātithiḥ paścāt sa rājan ketanakṣamaḥ
english: One who first earned his wealth by the harsh labours of tillage, and who afterward becomes hospitable to all guests—he, O king, is fit to be invited.

sanskrit: brahmavikrayanirdiṣṭaṃ striyā yac cārjitaṃ dhanam adeyaṃ pitṛdevebhyo yac ca klaibyād upārjitam
english: Wealth got by the selling of sacred knowledge, wealth earned by a woman, and wealth gained through unmanliness—these are not to be given to the ancestors and the gods.

sanskrit: kriyamāṇe 'pavarge tu yo dvijo bharatarṣabha na vyāharati yad yuktaṃ tasyādharmo gavānṛtam
english: When the concluding rite is being performed, the twice-born who does not utter what is fitting, O bull of the Bhāratas—his transgression is as the falsehood that loses a cow.

sanskrit: śrāddhasya brāhmaṇaḥ kālaḥ prāptaṃ dadhi ghṛtaṃ tathā somakṣayaś ca māṃsaṃ ca yad āraṇyaṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: The brāhmaṇa is the right occasion for the śrāddha; fit also are curds and clarified butter when they come to hand, the waning of the moon, and the flesh of forest game, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: śrāddhāpavarge viprasya svadhā vai svaditā bhavet kṣatriyasyāpy atho brūyāt prīyantāṃ pitaras tv iti
english: At the conclusion of a brāhmaṇa's śrāddha, let the word svadhā be well pronounced; for a kṣatriya, too, let him then say, "May the ancestors be pleased."

sanskrit: apavarge tu vaiśyasya śrāddhakarmaṇi bhārata akṣayyam abhidhātavyaṃ svasti śūdrasya bhārata
english: At the conclusion of a vaiśya's śrāddha rite, O Bhārata, the word "imperishable" is to be spoken; and for a śūdra, "well-being," O Bhārata.

sanskrit: puṇyāhavācanaṃ daive brāhmaṇasya vidhīyate etad eva niroṃkāraṃ kṣatriyasya vidhīyate vaiśyasya caiva vaktavyaṃ prīyantāṃ devatā iti
english: In the offering to the gods, the proclamation of an auspicious day is ordained for the brāhmaṇa; this same proclamation, without the syllable Oṃ, is ordained for the kṣatriya; and for the vaiśya it is to be spoken thus: "May the deities be pleased."

sanskrit: karmaṇām ānupūrvīṃ ca vidhipūrvakṛtaṃ śṛṇu jātakarmādikān sarvāṃs triṣu varṇeṣu bhārata brahmakṣatre hi mantroktā vaiśyasya ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: Hear now the due sequence of the rites and their prescribed performance—all the sacraments beginning with the birth-rite among the three varṇas, O Bhārata; for the brāhmaṇa and the kṣatriya they are enjoined with sacred chants, and so too for the vaiśya, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: viprasya raśanā mauñjī maurvī rājanyagāminī bālvajīty eva vaiśyasya dharma eṣa yudhiṣṭhira
english: For the brāhmaṇa the girdle is of muñja grass, for the kṣatriya it is of bowstring fibre, and for the vaiśya it is of balbaja grass—such is the law, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: dātuḥ pratigrahītuś ca dharmādharmāv imau śṛṇu brāhmaṇasyānṛte 'dharmaḥ proktaḥ pātakasaṃjñitaḥ caturguṇaḥ kṣatriyasya vaiśyasyāṣṭaguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Hear now, of the giver and the receiver alike, these their dharma and their transgression: for the brāhmaṇa, the sin in falsehood is declared to bear the name of a grievous fault; for the kṣatriya it is held to be fourfold, and for the vaiśya eightfold.

sanskrit: nānyatra brāhmaṇo 'śnīyāt pūrvaṃ vipreṇa ketitaḥ yavīyān paśuhiṃsāyāṃ tulyadharmo bhavet sa hi
english: A brāhmaṇa, if invited beforehand by another brāhmaṇa, should not eat elsewhere; for the younger man who does so incurs a guilt equal to the slaughter of an animal.

sanskrit: atha rājanyavaiśyābhyāṃ yady aśnīyāt tu ketitaḥ yavīyān paśuhiṃsāyāṃ bhāgārdhaṃ samavāpnuyāt
english: But if, being invited, he should eat at the homes of a kṣatriya or a vaiśya, the younger man thereby incurs half the share of the guilt of slaying an animal.

sanskrit: daivaṃ vāpy atha vā pitryaṃ yo 'śnīyād brāhmaṇādiṣu asnāto brāhmaṇo rājaṃs tasyādharmo gavānṛtam
english: The brāhmaṇa who eats at the rite for the gods or for the ancestors, in the houses of brāhmaṇas and the rest, while yet unbathed, O king—his transgression is as the falsehood that loses a cow.

sanskrit: āśauco brāhmaṇo rājan yo 'śnīyād brāhmaṇādiṣu jñānapūrvam atho lobhāt tasyādharmo gavānṛtam
english: The brāhmaṇa who, while in a state of impurity, eats in the houses of brāhmaṇas and the rest, knowingly and out of greed, O king—his transgression is as the falsehood that loses a cow.

sanskrit: annenānnaṃ ca yo lipset karmārthaṃ caiva bhārata āmantrayati rājendra tasyādharmo 'nṛtaṃ smṛtam
english: He who would seek food in return for food, and who invites another merely for the sake of his own rite, O Bhārata, O lord of kings—his transgression is reckoned to be a falsehood.

sanskrit: avedavratacāritrās tribhir varṇair yudhiṣṭhira mantravat pariviṣyante teṣv adharmo gavānṛtam
english: Those wanting in the Vedas, in vows, and in good conduct, who are served as if entitled to the sacred chants by the three varṇas, O Yudhiṣṭhira—in their case the transgression is as the falsehood that loses a cow.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pitryaṃ vāpy atha vā daivaṃ dīyate yat pitāmaha etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ dattaṃ yeṣu mahāphalam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of that which is given at the rite for the ancestors or for the gods, grandfather, I wish to hear in whom a gift bestowed bears great fruit.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yeṣāṃ dārāḥ pratīkṣante suvṛṣṭim iva karṣakāḥ uccheṣapariśeṣaṃ hi tān bhojaya yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: Those whose wives await the leavings and remnants of the meal as tillers await a good rain—feed them, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: cāritraniyatā rājan ye kṛśāḥ kṛśavṛttayaḥ arthinaś copagacchanti teṣu dattaṃ mahāphalam
english: Those steadfast in good conduct, O king, who are lean and whose means are meagre, and who come as suppliants—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

sanskrit: tadbhaktās tadgṛhā rājaṃs taddhanās tadapāśrayāḥ arthinaś ca bhavanty arthe teṣu dattaṃ mahāphalam
english: Those who are devoted to you, who dwell in your house, O king, whose wealth and whose refuge lie in you, and who come as suppliants in their need—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

sanskrit: taskarebhyaḥ parebhyo vā ye bhayārtā yudhiṣṭhira arthino bhoktum icchanti teṣu dattaṃ mahāphalam
english: Those who, distressed by fear of thieves or of enemies, O Yudhiṣṭhira, come as suppliants desiring to eat—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

sanskrit: akalkakasya viprasya bhaikṣotkarakṛtātmanaḥ baṭavo yasya bhikṣanti tebhyo dattaṃ mahāphalam
english: The young students who beg on behalf of a guileless brāhmaṇa, one who has shaped his soul by living on gleaned alms—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

sanskrit: hṛtasvā hṛtadārāś ca ye viprā deśasaṃplave arthārtham abhigacchanti tebhyo dattaṃ mahāphalam
english: Those brāhmaṇas who, robbed of their goods and bereft of their wives in the ruin of a land, come seeking aid—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

sanskrit: vratino niyamasthāś ca ye viprāḥ śrutasaṃmatāḥ tatsamāptyartham icchanti teṣu dattaṃ mahāphalam
english: Those brāhmaṇas observing vows and firm in their restraints, esteemed for their sacred learning, who desire help for the completion of those vows—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

sanskrit: avyutkrāntāś ca dharmeṣu pāṣaṇḍasamayeṣu ca kṛśaprāṇāḥ kṛśadhanās teṣu dattaṃ mahāphalam
english: Those who have never strayed from the dharmas into the doctrines of heretics, whose vital strength is wasted and whose wealth is meagre—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

sanskrit: kṛtasarvasvaharaṇā nirdoṣāḥ prabhaviṣṇubhiḥ spṛhayanti ca bhuktānnaṃ teṣu dattaṃ mahāphalam
english: Those who, though blameless, have been stripped of all their possessions by the powerful, and who long for a meal of food—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

sanskrit: tapasvinas taponiṣṭhās teṣāṃ bhaikṣacarāś ca ye arthinaḥ kiṃ cid icchanti teṣu dattaṃ mahāphalam
english: The ascetics steadfast in austerity, and those of them who wander seeking alms, who as suppliants desire some little thing—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

sanskrit: mahāphalavidhir dāne śrutas te bharatarṣabha nirayaṃ yena gacchanti svargaṃ caiva hi tac chṛṇu
english: The rule of great fruit in giving you have now heard, O bull of the Bhāratas; now hear that by which men go to hell, and likewise to heaven.

sanskrit: gurvarthaṃ vābhayārthaṃ vā varjayitvā yudhiṣṭhira ye 'nṛtaṃ kathayanti sma te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Save for the sake of one's teacher or to save a life, O Yudhiṣṭhira, those who utter falsehood—they indeed are bound for hell.

sanskrit: paradārābhihartāraḥ paradārābhimarśinaḥ paradāraprayoktāras te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those who carry off the wives of others, who lay hands upon the wives of others, and who procure the wives of others—they indeed are bound for hell.

sanskrit: ye parasvāpahartāraḥ parasvānāṃ ca nāśakāḥ sūcakāś ca pareṣāṃ ye te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those who seize away the goods of others, who destroy the goods of others, and who are informers against others—they indeed are bound for hell.

sanskrit: prapāṇāṃ ca sabhānāṃ ca saṃkramāṇāṃ ca bhārata agārāṇāṃ ca bhettāro narā nirayagāminaḥ
english: The men who are destroyers of watering-sheds, of assembly halls, of bridges and causeways, and of houses, O Bhārata—they are bound for hell.
